The Basel Problem

A staircase of reciprocal squares climbs toward one flat plane. The height of that plane is the famous answer.

Each new step of the partial sums is smaller than the one before. So the staircase piles up toward a definite height. The surprise is that π hides inside that height. Why π appears at all is only sketched at the idea level.

For example, stack 📦 boxes under a line drawn on a wall. The boxes shrink until the stack creeps so close to the line that your eye cannot see the gap.

∑n=1∞1n2=π26\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\frac{1}{n^2}=\frac{\pi^2}{6}n=1∑∞​n21​=6π2​

Derive ∑n=1∞1(2n)2=π224\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\frac{1}{(2n)^2} = \frac{\pi^2}{24}∑n=1∞​(2n)21​=24π2​ from the Basel sum.

∑n=1∞1(2n)2=14∑n=1∞1n2=π224\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\frac{1}{(2n)^2}=\frac{1}{4}\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\frac{1}{n^2}=\frac{\pi^2}{24}n=1∑∞​(2n)21​=41​n=1∑∞​n21​=24π2​
Show proof

  1. 1(2n)2=14⋅1n2\frac{1}{(2n)^2} = \frac{1}{4}\cdot\frac{1}{n^2}(2n)21​=41​⋅n21​.

  2. For a positive-term series constants factor out, so ∑n=1∞1(2n)2=14∑n=1∞1n2=14⋅π26=π224\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\frac{1}{(2n)^2} = \frac{1}{4}\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\frac{1}{n^2} = \frac{1}{4}\cdot\frac{\pi^2}{6} = \frac{\pi^2}{24}∑n=1∞​(2n)21​=41​∑n=1∞​n21​=41​⋅6π2​=24π2​.

Derive ∑k=0∞1(2k+1)2=π28\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\frac{1}{(2k+1)^2} = \frac{\pi^2}{8}∑k=0∞​(2k+1)21​=8π2​.

∑odd1n2=π26−π224=π28\sum_{\mathrm{odd}}\frac{1}{n^2}=\frac{\pi^2}{6}-\frac{\pi^2}{24}=\frac{\pi^2}{8}odd∑​n21​=6π2​−24π2​=8π2​
Show proof

  1. A positive-term series splits into (even terms) + (odd terms).

  2. Hence the odd sum =π26−π224=4π2−π224=3π224=π28= \frac{\pi^2}{6} - \frac{\pi^2}{24} = \frac{4\pi^2-\pi^2}{24} = \frac{3\pi^2}{24} = \frac{\pi^2}{8}=6π2​−24π2​=244π2−π2​=243π2​=8π2​.
